chapter_title: Concerning the Four Fathers; what they are like.
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly a systematic correspondential teaching (body-faculties mapped to cosmic beings/structures). The only clear late layer is the dialogue/lecture framing: the opening attribution to “the apostle…to his disciples” and the closing “Behold, I have shown to you…”. No Gospel citation formulae or institutional (church) applications appear; “Jesus the Splendour” functions as a cosmological being, not NT overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as the corporeal body has limbs that are hidden, so it also has others that are visible. They can be seen upon it, they can be grasped and receive blows and wounds, whilst others can neither be grasped nor receive blows.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:” (hagiographic compilation frame; ‘apostle’ is a Layer-2 marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core teaching begins immediately after the frame attribution: impersonal analogy of hidden/visible limbs as a structural setup for later cosmos↔body mappings.

paragraphs.core_text: So it is also with this entire greatness, as we resemble it. Some of it is hidden, whilst some of it is visible; some of it is far away from the blows and suffering, whilst some of it receives blows and wounds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, system-internal analogy: ‘greatness’ (cosmic totality) mapped to hidden/visible states and susceptibility to ‘blows/wounds’ (suffering mechanics), without institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, thus the directive of the body that lives within, hidden in the storehouses inside the body and unseen. So it is also how the Father, the God of truth, exists; as he too is hidden in his kingdom, not displayed before this outer desolation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct correspondential mapping (body’s inner directive faculty ↔ the Father hidden in his kingdom). Both sides remain within cosmic/anthropic system; no audience-address or ecclesial identification.

paragraphs.core_text: Thus, too, the body has two eyes that are visible and seen, and are even the body's source of illumination; so there are also these two light ships that shine and are seen in the entire universe and the whole of creation. The light has never been hidden, just like the two eyes of the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic substrate pattern: organ-function correspondence (eyes/illumination) mapped to cosmic structures (two Light Ships in the universe). Impersonal, systematic exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The living soul too is like this; it is established in apparent silence. In its apparent silence it is grasped and receives blows from these five fleshes, which destroy (the soul) and strike it. It can be likened to the mystery of the corporeal body, as it can be grasped and mastered, can receive blows and wounds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic suffering mechanism stated as process (soul receiving blows from the five fleshes) and mapped to bodily vulnerability; remains within the cosmological drama, not moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, thus this tongue that speaks, proclaims, reprimands and reveals about everything happening in this body, inside and outside, also the considerations and bodily knowledges. The tongue, which is outside, makes it manifest. It also proclaims about the honour and shame of the body. And it speaks, unveiling the pain of the body that is sick from its sores.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still the correspondential substrate: functional description of the tongue as revealer/manifestor, preparing the next mapping to a cosmic revealer. No NT citation or pastoral address.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also what Jesus the Splendour is like, who shall be sent from the greatness. He manifests and reveals about everything, both the external and the internal, both what is above and what is below. Be it about the outer aeons that are hidden and not displayed, or about the ships of light that are seen: he is the one who unveils about them. He is also the one who reveals about their glory, and the greatness that dwells in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: ‘Jesus the Splendour’ functions as a defined cosmological revealer (tongue-correspondence continued), not as a Gospel-cited Jesus. The mapping remains cosmos↔faculty↔cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: And regarding this beating and wounding of the living soul, Jesus is the one who reveals it. He also preaches about (the soul) and its peace. He reveals about its cleansing and healing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the same cosmic function: revelation of the soul’s wounding and its restoration. ‘Preaches’ appears as functional vocabulary (revealer role), without NT quotation or institutional discipline.
Second-person summative closure (‘Behold, I have shown to you…’) typical of editorial/homiletic framing that wraps the teaching rather than expounding new cosmological correspondences.
